# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
...

# OfficeHQ

A full-stack office-management web application.

- **Front end:** React single-page app (TypeScript) with TanStack Router (file-based routes) and
  TanStack Query, built into `src/main/resources/static`.
- **Back end:** Spring Boot host with OfficeFloor REST endpoints, on an in-memory H2 database with
  Flyway migrations run on boot.

## Build and run

```
bin/build              # build the SPA and package one runnable jar
PORT=3000 bin/start    # start the app (serves the SPA + REST on $PORT)
bin/stop               # stop it
```

Readiness: `GET /actuator/health`.

## Tests

End-to-end tests use Playwright (in `e2e/`) and bind to `data-testid`:

```
bin/e2e                # build, start, run the specs in e2e/specs, then stop
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the whole app into ONE runnable jar: the Maven build compiles the front-end
# (frontend-maven-plugin) into src/main/resources/static, then packages the Spring Boot app
# (spring-boot repackage, main net.officefloor.hq.app.Application) into target/*.jar.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# `clean` first so removed sources (e.g. a deleted route .yml or class) can't linger in
# target/classes and get baked into the jar.
exec ./mvnw -q -DskipTests clean package
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the whole app into ONE runnable jar: the Maven build compiles the front-end
# (frontend-maven-plugin) into src/main/resources/static, then packages the Spring Boot app
# (spring-boot repackage, main net.officefloor.hq.app.Application) into target/*.jar.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# `clean` first so removed sources (e.g. a deleted route .yml or class) can't linger in
# target/classes and get baked into the jar.
exec ./mvnw -q -DskipTests clean package
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

content.text:
People can now be retired from a date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass on the first run.

**What changed**

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V15__person_retired.sql`, adds a `retired_from` date to each person (empty means not retired). Each person sent to the screen now also carries `retired` and `retiredFrom`.
- **Retiring:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire`, takes `{from}`. If the date is blank it uses the sheet's today. It saves the date, then writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=… by=… name=… from=…` to the audit file. A bad date is refused with nothing written. Retiring doesn't change the person's version, and it writes no rollup line, since no total changes.
- **Claim rule:** a claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused, with the reason shown in the claim form's error. This applies in three places: adding a claim from the row, the quick-add bar, and editing a claim. Claims dated on or before the retirement date are still allowed, including ones added later.
- **Screen** (`People.tsx`):
  - A "show retired" checkbox (`show-retired`), kept in the URL as `showRetired`. It's off when the screen first opens, and loading a sheet doesn't change it.
  - Retired people's rows are hidden unless the checkbox is on. Their claims still count in the due total and the claimed total.
  - Each row shows `person-retired` (yes/no) and `person-retired-from`, with a date field and a Retire button.
  - Statement and retire share the row's single `person-error` element, and taking either action clears it.

**Choices the request didn't settle**

- Retiring someone already retired just moves their date; it isn't refused.
- Claims already dated after the retirement date stay as they are. Retiring isn't refused because of them, and one of the test scenarios relies on this.
- Editing a claim is only checked when its date actually changes. So an existing claim dated after retirement can still be edited if its date stays the same.
